newsitem.title: UK: Dry cargo freight steady on Atlantic shortages.
newsitem.headline: Dry cargo freight steady on Atlantic shortages.

text.p: The basic trends in the dry cargo freight market remain unchanged with the BFI up 5 points to 1523 on Thursday.
There is a shortage of early Panamaxes in the Atlantic where rates continue firm but may now be affected by tonnage in ballast in the Pacific opting to fix business from US gulf.
There is evidence that rates for trans-pacific business are falling for Panamaxes but fixtures from Australia, S.Africa and East Coast South America are more stable, brokers said.
The Pacific is still strong for capers, but conditions are less predictable in the atlantic.
Handies continued to flourish from the plate but elsewhere, especially from the Continent, rates are steady at best.

GRAIN - Cargill's fixture of Maratha Majesty for 63,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Holland for Dec/Jan at $14.90 was a significant increase on last done in this size, Kapitan Spivak at the end of last week for Dec 20/30 at $13.65, also by Cargill.
New Panamax grain business quoted today included Dreyfus with a spot order of 50/55,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Egyptian Med and Toepfer with 50,000 heavy grain St Lawrence/Continent for Jan 11/20.
For some reason Bobilna 64,584 dwt did not proceed with her fixture with MISR for a transatlantic round and is now reported fixed delivery prompt Flushing for a trip to the Far East at $13,000 daily.

Gortys 71,504 dwt is rumoured fixed delivery Continent early Jan for 12 months to European charterers at $11,000/11,250 daily. In the North Pacific Continental's fixture of Lucky Bulker for 50,000 heavy grain to S.Korea for Jan 5/15 at $13.50 indicated a decline in this trade.

By comparison brokers reported the Australian market to be firmer and Indian charterers were said to have booked 2 Panamaxes and 2 vessels of 30/40,000 dwt on subjects with grain on voyage basis loading Dec/Jan from Australia to India.

Nephele 70,000 dwt was linked with Emirates Trading from S. Australia to Bin Qasim but details were lacking. In the handy-sizes the over-age Leros Progress 28,000 dwt was reported fixed delivery Recalada Dec 20/25 trip via Med redelivery Gibraltar at a firm $7,300 daily plus $130,000 bonus (possibly by continental to Tunisia or Algeria).

In addition to Andre's fixture of Orgullo for 25,000 wheat up River/Algeria at $30.00, Olympia was rumoured fixed for similar business (possibly also by Continental). Glencore were linked with a 15,900 dwt vessel delivery Recalada trip Skaw-Passero $4,350 daily plus unknown bonus.

Other reported grain business included Woodlark for 16,000 wheat La Pallice/Casablanca for prompt shipment at $17.00. Toepfer quoted fresh handy-size business with 25,000 wheat Up River/Tunisia for Jan 14/21 and 1.6-1.7m cft Mississippi/Continent for Jan 3/13.

MINERALS - Rumours of recent Caper period fixtures have begun to emerge with Hanjin having fixed Anangel Solidarity 161,545 dwt in direct continuation from April/May for 2 years, the first at $14,000/14,250 daily and the second in the $16,000's.

Halla were linked with Anangel Ambition 150,264 dwt also delivery April for 12 months in the low $14,000's daily. China Steel were understood to have booked U Ming Caper tonnage to Kaohsiung from W.Australia with ironore at $4.05, option coal from Queensland at about $5.00/5.25 or New South Wales at $5.95.
Korea Line were on subjects with a Caper from Richards Bay to 2 ports Denmark for January.

Docenave fixed a Caper on private terms in the east for 2 laden legs via Australia to the Atlantic. In the Panamax category Tatry 66,000 dwt failed with K Line on account of dates for a trip from N.Spain via Narvik with ironore to Cigading at $15,000 daily.
British Steel fixed 70,000 coal Mobile/Port Talbot for early Jan at close to $8.25. Nordbulk was reckoned fixed by K line for an Australian round but details were not available.
Daiichi fixed the Halla-relet Achilles 68,000 dwt delivery Okinawa early Jan trip via Australia to Japan $11,750 daily.

HANDIES - The Continent continued to be a weak market for these vessels. Jebsen fixed a 30,000 dwt vessel from Norway via the Continent to E.Africa on private terms. Nea Doxa 30,000 dwt was closely working prompt N.France trip India at about $9,200 daily with cargo Levant. In the far east Capetan Michalis 28,500 dwt was taken by Clipper delivery Malaysia trip via W.Australia to Taiwan at $6,300 daily and Anangel Honesty 31,000 dwt fixed and failed on subjects with S.Korean charterers delivery Singapore trip via Australia to the far East at $6,500 daily.
Daiichi booked Pacific Power 42,000 dwt delivery Yantai Dec 23/29 trip via China to Japan at $8,000 daily and Moonlight Success 27,000 dwt delivery Taiwan trip S.Korea on private terms.
